Dear SCSF Member,

Well, here we are again, at that time of year when we need to start thinking about renewing for the  coming season, 2025-26, which begins on July 1, 2025. Unless you have renewed prior to then, your  current membership will expire with SCSF and USFS.

USFS is going to raise our fees again this season. Since our home club rates last season were the same  as Pre-Covid rates, we will have a nominal increase ($10) in our rates to cover the added expense when  registering our members.

We will be opening up the Entryeeze system for renewals beginning May 18th, 2025. If you’ve never been  a member of USFS and you are just joining the club, please remember that your membership with USFS  begins on July 1, 2025. Introductory members will not be able to sign up for tests or competitions until  that date. If you are already a club member, your current membership is good until June 30th, so you are  covered for testing and competing straight through.
Renew early to get the most out of your membership, but whatever you do, renew before June 30, 2025 in order to vote in the club election which is upcoming this summer.

PLEASE MAKE SURE, when renewing this year, you take a moment to update your contact information, using these links, both in EntryEeze and then on the USFS site in Members Only, and check the following:
Spelling of names must be exactly the same on both sites and any applications you put in to  compete. If they are different the system flags them as unverifiable.
Check your phone numbers and email addresses and update if there are any changes to either. We  need to be able to contact you efficiently!

Check to make sure you have your USFS number entered in your Entryeeze account. If you are an  Introductory member, you can get your number from me at membership@scsf.org and then put it  into your account.

If you are a Home Club member and you also skate on a team, please remember that you must have  at least one Parent membership with SCSF. You cannot be a parent member of SCSF if your child has a home club elsewhere!

Watch for information and updates from the club in our club newsletter and through Entryeeze emails.  This past year has been a great season for our athletes! We hosted two very successful competitions with  NQS Skate SF 2024 and ‘Skate SF 2024 2.0’, along with our equally successful Annual Gala!

We look forward to an even more successful year and would love for you to, once again, be there with us!  And so, on behalf of the Board of Directors of The Skating Club of San Francisco, Inc., Welcome back to what’s sure to be another exciting season with the SCSF!
Warm Regards,

Officials Support Application

Purpose: The purpose of this policy is to encourage prospective officials and support existing officials with expenses incurred for their education and training for USFS / ISU sponsored training seminars and trial judging at designated non-qualifying and qualifying competitions.

Eligibility:  Applicants must be SCSF Home Club members for three (3) consecutive years and have received approval to participate in an official seminar and/or trial judge at a designated event.  Expenses eligible for reimbursement include fees for seminars and trial judging along with travel and food expenses as defined by the USFS Travel Policy.   Total expenses for an individual applicant are subject to a maximum amount defined by the Board on an annual basis.

Approval Process:  The applicant will notify the Board by email of their intent to register for participation in a seminar and/or trial judging event and subsequent approval to attend their requested event.  Upon completion of the their attendance, the applicant will submit the standard USFS Expense Form with attached receipts directly to the Board for approval at the next scheduled Board meeting.

SCSF Volunteer Commitment
Background

Our Club is run entirely by volunteers. Without volunteers, our Club would not exist as we’d have no one to manage the Club at the Board level, or be able to host events including test sessions, critiques, competitions (e.g., Skate San Francisco, Pacific Coast Adult Sectionals), and our fund-raising Gala.
Volunteer Hour Commitment

SCSF has instituted a new commitment request for volunteer hours supplied by its members. Club events and operations require considerable amounts of preparation and execution time, all done by volunteers. This is true for clubs across the country, many of whom have formal volunteer hour commitments or policies in place.

In an effort to get our members engaged to help, the Club has instituted a new ‘volunteer commitment’ that every member, or family, should participate in and contribute to each season. Simply put, the commitment states that we are asking every member to donate 2 hours of your time helping out at a Club event or activity. Any family with 3 or more members should volunteer a minimum of 5 hours total.

These hours can count toward any volunteer hours that may be required by members for various different reasons, such as school applications, etc. The Club will be happy to document volunteer hours required for school or other community service activities.
Volunteer Opportunities
Volunteering is a positive experience, a chance to have some fun and get connected with the Club and its members. We are hoping people will want to help out…it feels good to help!

There will be many opportunities, so it shouldn’t be difficult for members to meet this obligation. Some of these opportunities could be at Skate SF, the Gala, test sessions, attending the annual meeting…any in person club activity that requires someone to spend time preparing for to make it happen.
It’s a great way to help out, get involved, meet other club members, make new friends and contacts…and have some fun at the same time!
Volunteer Tracking

Every event will have a chairperson, or someone in charge, who will have a list of the volunteers who have signed up. When you have completed your shift, you simply have the person in charge at the event check you off as having fulfilled your shift with the number of hours donated. The chairperson with give this information to the Membership Chair who will record and track the hours in your Entryeeze account. You can check on your hours any time you wish.
Volunteer Hours Unfulfilled?

You weren’t able to fulfill your volunteer commitment? No problem! We are asking any member or family who was unable to fulfill their volunteer commitment hours by the end of the season, to make a tax-deductible donation to our Hickox Memorial Fund, in lieu of their hours…suggested minimum of $50, or whatever you can afford. These donations will go directly back to athlete support programs. In this way, you can still take part in the process and commitment to supporting our athletes.
Volunteering is Rewarding

Volunteering can be very rewarding, and even fun, and it leaves you with a very good feeling afterward knowing that you’ve helped someone out! It is the hope of the SCSF that every member will step up and pitch in to help with our club events as part of a team to make these events fun and enjoyable, for all our members.

There are many, many age-appropriate tasks and duties at our events to fit the ages of any of our members, and no amount of help is too little! All will be appreciated immensely and with your contribution of help and time, our skating club and community will be working as a team and that much better for it!

The SCSF Coaches Support Policy

The SCSF Coaches Support Policy is designed to help facilitate the betterment of our coaches through educational events and continued training programs presented by US Figure Skating, and to help alleviate the burden of some annual expenses incurred by our professional coaches, by providing financial support for eligible expenses.
Please see the following for details on eligibility and procedures for applications.

Eligibility: To be eligible for financial support, a coach must have been a SCSF Coach or Home Club Adult member for a minimum of 3 consecutive years prior to any application for reimbursement, and must be a current member in good standing with SCSF in the year the application is submitted. Coaching must be their major source of income, not a side job. The coach must be both self-designated as a coach and coach-compliant with US Figure Skating, and must also maintain, at minimum, a USFS Accreditation in any discipline. In addition, a coach applying for financial support must have volunteered a minimum of 5 hours total at any club sponsored events or club operations, for the fiscal year in which the application is submitted, if such events are available.

Expenses: Expenses eligible for reimbursement include registration fees for seminars, conference/summit, ratings, etc. and associated travel expenses such as airfare and hotel. Other expenses eligible are annual expenses for items including, but not limited to, CEUs, Liability Insurance, Coach I.C.E., etc. To be eligible, expenses must be directly related to the coaching occupation or to an eligible coach’s education event through either US Figure Skating or other recognized figure skating organization (ex. ISI or Skate Canada). Food and beverage expenses will not be considered. Membership fees paid to SCSF are not reimbursable expenses, nor are any monies or fees paid to SCSF for any reason.

Procedure: The coach must submit an application to the Board, through any current board member, outlining the nature of the request, detailing the breakdown of the expenses involved, the event, date, location if applicable, and any other information pertinent to the application. Original receipts in the applicant’s own name must be provided by the coach for all applications for financial support under this policy. Applications must be submitted in the same fiscal year (Sept. 1 – Aug. 31) in which the expenses are incurred. It is the coach’s responsibility to obtain proof of volunteer hours from the Club for the application and to make sure all criteria are met.

Reimbursement Amounts: The amount of the reimbursement is based on the coaches SCSF membership category (i.e. SCSF Coach or Home Club Adult) and on the level of the coach’s USFS accreditation. The total amount that any one individual may be reimbursed for expenses for an application is subject to a maximum limit decided annually by the Board, and will be a tiered percentage of that limit, based further on the level of any USFS accreditations held by the coach. (Ex. A Home Club Adult Member may be eligible for 100% of the max. amount, whereas an SCSF Coach Member eligible for 80% of max. amount. Additionally, this amount will be subject to a tiered percentage based on USFS accreditations from Master, Senior, Level 2, or Level 1, at 100%, 80%, 60%, or 40% percent, respectively.)

The Skating Club of San Francisco, Inc. Board of Directors

Candidate Biographies for the Board Election
Diane Zhou

I’m Diane Zhou, a current board member running for re-election. During my 2023-2025 term, I led the planning committee for our annual gala which raised thousands of dollars to support our skaters, streamlined our monthly virtual testing process to reduce overhead and errors, and represented SCSF at the US Figure Skating Governing Council where I exchanged valuable insights and ideas with other clubs. My previous leadership experience in the figure skating world includes overseeing logistics and expanding opportunities in the MIT Figure Skating Club as the president and a choreographer, and helping to establish San Francisco Ice Theatre’s inaugural adult team as the captain in their first two years. I am also a 3x USFS Gold Medalist (Skating Skills, Singles, Solo Dance Follow) and the 2025 Adult Nationals Championship Masters Junior-Senior Women’s silver medalist.

I’m no stranger to the physical, mental, and logistical challenges that come with figure skating, and I believe that this sport cannot be pursued sustainably in isolation. As a board member, I’ve done my best to consider not only skaters’ needs but also the impact on parents, family, coaches, judges, officials, rink staff, volunteers, and fellow board members, whose dedication makes skating opportunities possible. Looking ahead, I remain committed to refining processes to be more efficient, consistent, and transparent, so that we can all devote more of our time and energy toward SCSF’s mission to provide an environment where every individual skater can realize their own potential. I am so grateful to be part of a community that fuels personal growth both on and off the ice, and I would be honored to continue serving the SCSF board!
Don Corbiell

I began playing hockey when I was 4 (I grew up in Canada!) and then switched to figure skating when I was 11 years old. I have been ice skating for 56 years now! I am a current US Figure Skating double Master rated coach in both Singles (Freestyle) and Skating Skills (Moves in the Field). Previously, I was a PSA (Professional Skater’s Association) double Master Rated coach, a PSA examiner, sat on the PSA Board of Governors, was the past PSA Seminars Chair, and was on the PSA National Education Committee. I was also fortunate enough to be asked to be a presenter at the PSA conferences in Chicago, Palm Springs, and again in Las Vegas.

San Francisco is now my home. More locally, I have been coaching for over 30 years in the San Francisco/Bay Area, serving as the Membership Chair for SCSF for well over a decade, and helping out with the Test Chair duties when needed. Currently, it has also been my pleasure to serve as the President of the SCSF Board of Directors and, for the past 5 years, to work with the strong and vibrant board that we have.

I still love the sport that I fell in love with all those many years ago, and, along with skating, I like to say that I try to teach my students to be well…well educated, well spoken, well rounded, well mannered, and well adjusted!

I would very much like to continue my work as President and Membership Chair on the Board of Directors, and continue to help foster an atmosphere of inclusion for all of our members. I still have many ideas to offer our community, and I hope you will put a check next to my name when you vote in this year’s election!
Thank you for your time, and for participating in the election!
Alyssa Lewis
I am a figure skating coach and have been teaching in the Bay Area for over 20 years. I am a USFS Double Gold Medallist and USFS Accredited Senior coach. I began skating in Hawai

’i when I was seven and have spent most of my life in the figure skating world. Prior to coaching full-time, I managed Belmont Iceland for 8 years. During that time, I joined the Skating Club of San Francisco and worked closely with the club to put on the annual Silver Spin Competition, the Gala fundraiser, and to create a positive club community in Belmont.

For the last four years, I’ve enjoyed being a member of the board and managing the testing program for the club. During my first term, I worked with the previous test chair to get our Virtual Testing Program started. When the chair stepped down from the Board, I took over as Test Chair. The testing program has grown so much that last year, I brought on two more of our board members to oversee the virtual testing portion. This season I’ve also helped organize feedback sessions, which give our skaters the opportunity to hear directly from local judges about what to improve in their skating; and performance practice exhibitions, which give skaters the chance to skate their program on the ice by themselves in a performance setting.
I am honored to run again for the club board and to continue organizing opportunities for all of our skaters.
Jean Teng
Hello fellow SCSF members,
My name is Jean Teng and I am the current Vice President of the Skating Club of San Francisco – a role I have served in for the last six years.

For those of you who don’t know me, I took up skating as an adult 16 years ago and immediately fell in love. Since then, I have actively competed on the adult level both nationally and internationally. Drawn by the sense of camaraderie and community, I hope to continue giving back to the sport that has given me so much.

Outside of skating, I am an attorney by profession. After several years of law firm life, I now work as an independent contractor focused on legal research and writing (which, not coincidentally, also allows more time for skating!). I live in San Francisco with my husband who doubles as an excellent skating cheerleader. I love to travel and cheer on our Bay Area sports teams (go Giants, Niners, and Warriors!).

I believe my experience as an active competitive adult skater who has strong ties to the international adult skating community brings a unique perspective to our board and club. I hope you will allow me to continue serving this community!

This Basic Support Program (BSP) available to all SCSF Home Club members updates the "Competitors’ Support Policy" previously adopted by the SCSF Board. This Basic Support Program will be published for all SCSF members to view. This BSP covers the following categories:

I. Well-Balanced (Championship Track) Non-Elite, Singles, Dance and Pair Competitions
II. Elite Skaters
III. Adults
IV. National Excel Series
V. National Solo Dance
VI. National Showcase
VII. Synchronized Teams
VIII. Theatre on Ice
IX. Determination of Award Amounts and Payment of Awards
I. Well-Balanced (Championship Track) Non-Elite, Singles, Dance and Pair Competitions

A travel stipend will be provided to skaters who qualify for, and compete in, Sectional and United States Figure Skating Championships, excluding elite skaters who will be covered separately. The amount of the travel stipend will be determined by the overall available money in the support program fund for the year, the number of qualifying skaters, and the location of the competition for that season. The Board will identify and automatically disburse funds to eligible skaters.
Skaters who win Sectional or United States Figure Skating Championships will be awarded with a Club Membership for the next fiscal year.
All skaters who qualify for Sectionals Singles, the US Ice Dance Final, or US Pairs Final are eligible for a complimentary SCSF Competition Team warm-up jacket.
II. Elite Skaters

Elite skaters are defined as those who have competed in one or more elite Junior or Senior International (e.g. ISU Challenger Series or other qualifying International Event), ISU Championship, or qualifying US Championship events in the previous or current competitive season.

A travel stipend will be provided to skaters who compete in at least one Junior or Senior level qualifying international event. The amount of the travel stipend will be determined by the overall available money in the support program fund for the year, the number of qualifying skaters. The Board will identify and automatically disburse funds to eligible skaters.
Skaters who win Sectional or United States Figure Skating Championships will be awarded with a Club Membership for the next fiscal year.
III. Adults

A travel stipend will be provided to skaters who compete in a qualifying Championship event at the U.S. Adult Figure Skating Championships, provided they qualified through the corresponding event at the Sectional Championships with 6 or more competitors. The amount of the travel stipend will be determined by the overall available money in the support program fund for the year, the number of qualifying skaters, the number of championship events the skater qualifies in, and the location of the competition for that season. The Board will identify and automatically disburse funds to eligible skaters.
Adult skaters who win U.S. Adult Figure Skating Championships in a Championship event having 6 or more skaters will be awarded with a Club Membership for the next fiscal year.

All Adult skaters who compete at the Adult National Figure Skating Championships in a Championship event are eligible for a complimentary SCSF Adult Skating Team warm-up jacket, regardless of the number of competitors at the corresponding event at the Sectional Championships. If the skater opts out of the jacket, a substitute stipend will be provided.
IV. National Excel Series

A travel stipend will be provided to skaters who compete in the National Excel Final. The amount of the travel stipend will be determined by the overall available money in the support program fund for the year, the number of qualifying skaters, and the location of the competition for that season. The Board will identify and automatically disburse funds to eligible skaters.
Skaters who win an event at the National Excel Final in an event having 6 or more skaters will be awarded with a Club Membership for the next fiscal year.
All skaters who qualify for the National Excel Final are eligible for a complimentary SCSF Competition Team warm-up jacket. Proof of entry will be required.
V. National Solo Dance

A travel stipend will be provided to skaters who compete in the National Solo Dance Final. The amount of the travel stipend will be determined by the overall available money in the support program fund for the year, the number of qualifying skaters, the number of events the skater qualifies in, and the location of the competition for that season. The Board will identify and automatically disburse funds to eligible skaters.
Skaters who win a National Solo Dance Final event having 6 or more skaters will be awarded with a Club Membership for the next fiscal year.
All skaters who qualify for the National Solo Dance Final are eligible for a complimentary SCSF Competition Team warm-up jacket. Proof of entry will be required.
VI. National Showcase

A travel stipend will be provided to skaters who qualify for, and compete in, the Parade of Champions or the Parade of Adult Champions. The amount of the travel stipend will be determined by the overall available money in the support program fund for the year, the number of qualifying skaters, the number of events the skater qualifies in, and the location of the competition for that season. The Board will identify and automatically disburse funds to eligible skaters.
If a skater wins the Parade of Champions, they will receive a complimentary year membership with the club for the following season.
VII. Synchronized Skating Teams
Each non-qualifying Tremors team will receive a percentage of a maximum flat rate of $500 per team.
Each qualifying-level Tremors team will receive a percentage of a maximum flat rate of $1000 per team.
Any team advancing to the Synchronized Championships will receive a percentage of a maximum flat rate $500 bonus.

The percentage will be the same as the percentage of Home Club members on each team respectively. The board will automatically identify and disburse funds to all eligible teams. Receipts are no longer required. All skater and parent memberships must be current before funds can be disbursed.
VIII. Theatre on Ice Teams
